It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: Quadr II 17.1
div.ab: Ad quod aliquantulum pecunie uiaticum collegerat, et ipse dominus Ihesus loculos habebat, quicquid Eboracensium magnifica uanitas et malus semper inuidie liuor inerguminet.

note.seg: Girardus ecclesias nostras et homines et ipsum dominium nostrum multum pauperauit klagt Thomas, Gerhards Nachfolger, Anselmen, etwa August 1108 bei Eadmer Nov. IV, ed. Rule p. 200. Über die Feindschaft des Domcapitels aus finanziellen Gründen vgl. Will. Neuburg. I 3: in emungendis per indecoras etiam occasiones subditorum marsupiis callidus. Doch verzeichnet Hugo Sotovagina (ed. Raine p. 111 f.) Gerhards Verdienste um das Bistumsgut. Vgl. u. Anm. l

Girardus ecclesias nostras et homines et ipsum dominium nostrum multum pauperauit, complains Thomas, Gerard’s successor, to Anselm, about August 1108, in Eadmer Nov. IV, ed. Rule p. 200. On the hostility of the cathedral chapter for financial reasons cf. Will. Neuburg. I 3: in emungendis per indecoras etiam occasiones subditorum marsupiis callidus. Hugo Sotovagina (ed. Raine p. 111 f.), however, records Gerard’s services to the property of the see. Cf. below note l
‘to babble’, from inerguminus instead of energumenus

div.ab: For which he had collected a little money as provision for the journey; and the Lord Jesus himself had a purse, whatever the magnificent vanity of the men of York and the ever-evil spite of envy may rave.
